title: Smart Calendar App (Dribbble shot)
lede: A 2020 Dribbble concept for a calendar app in candy colors, cited in the article that named the style.
summary: Three frosted phone screens with light edges over a pink and lilac glow. Paperpillar, 2020.
made: 2020 (the screens show August 2020; cited by Malewicz in November 2020)

evidence.note: Inspected the shot image named in the page’s structured data (1600 × 1200, Dribbble CDN) in a scratchpad copy. Not stored. The page was read in Claude in Chrome; the cookie banner was not accepted. The exact post date was not visible on the page.

styles.note: A clear concept example from the Dribbble wave, cited by Malewicz for its 1 pt semi-transparent white outline that simulates the glass edge.

context: The Dribbble description reads “Calendar App exploration using some candy colors.” The shot is credited to Ghani Pradita for Paperpillar. [Dribbble](https://dribbble.com/shots/13842720-Smart-Calendar-App).
Malewicz calls it “a clear representation of this trend” and notes that it “may be on the verge of readability in some places”. [Malewicz 2020](ref:malewicz-glassmorphism-article-2020).
observed: The background is a soft glow of coral pink at the top fading into lilac at the upper right and white at the bottom.
Three tall phone screens are frosted panels: pink-tinted and translucent in their upper parts, near-opaque white in their lower cards.
Each panel and card has large rounded corners and a thin, lighter edge.
Colorful gradient spheres (Task, Notes, Event) sit on the third screen; the glass itself carries no imagery.
Text is a geometric sans-serif in dark plum. The primary buttons (‘Mulai’ and a plus button) are solid dark plum pills and discs.
interpretation: The shot matches all four diagnostic traits and also the ‘opaque primary action’ rule. It shows the Dribbble version of the style: presentation panels floating over a generated glow, not a real app screen.
borrow: Use near-opaque white for reading surfaces and more transparent tinted glass for headers.
Make the one primary button solid and dark so it reads through all the glass.

rights.statement: © Ghani Pradita / Paperpillar. No image is stored here.
